name: SE Ranking
subcategory: keyword research, backlinks and rank tracking
tagline: Track an owned keyword set and combine it with user-supplied audit and backlink files

pricing.notes: Typical Essential monthly rate; keyword count and check frequency change price.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For SE Ranking, track an owned keyword set and combine it with user-supplied audit and backlink files. The hard boundary is large ranking data operation, competitive research, white-label reporting, and integrations, plus proprietary web index and data acquisition.
coreLoopDIY: Track a user-supplied keyword set, collect permitted search-result snapshots at low volume, combine them with user-supplied audit and backlink files, and show trends without recreating a commercial web index.
requirements: approved search-data API or manual imports
whatYouLose: large ranking data operation, competitive research, white-label reporting, and integrations
moatNotes: proprietary web index and data acquisition
ongoingBurden: proxy and API costs, crawl freshness, geolocation, anti-bot rules, keyword normalization, storage, and data QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for SE Ranking because customers pay for a continuously refreshed web-scale dataset whose collection cost dwarfs the dashboard around it. The recurring cost buys proxy and API costs, crawl freshness, geolocation, anti-bot rules, keyword normalization, storage, and data QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: SerpBear
priorArt.desc: Open-source search ranking tracker for owned keyword sets.

alternatives.name: CrawlSEO
alternatives.desc: Owned-site crawls, rank snapshots, optional backlink data and alerts; capable software, decidedly non-trivial setup.

facts.install: Clone the repository, configure environment variables, and start its Docker/PostgreSQL stack
facts.engines: Uses Google Search Console and PageSpeed Insights for owned-site data, with optional DataForSEO credentials for keyword and backlink data; exposes MCP tools for compatible clients.
facts.dataFormat: Sites, crawl snapshots, issues, keyword/rank observations, alerts, task history, users, and OAuth tokens live in the self-hosted PostgreSQL database; crawled page content and reports are retained by that deployment rather than a vendor cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: CrawlSEO combines owned-site crawling and rank snapshots but has much thinner competitor research, backlink data, polished reports, collaboration, and managed data coverage than SE Ranking.
facts.setupBlocker: The first real obstacle is infrastructure plus identity: Docker and PostgreSQL, a public callback URL, and a Google Cloud OAuth application before Search Console-backed ranking and alerts work.

alternatives.name: OpenSEO
alternatives.desc: Rank tracking, audits, competitor rows and backlinks in one container; the backlink API is where free becomes philosophical.

facts.install: Clone the repository, supply environment variables, and run the documented Docker-based web/database deployment
facts.engines: Uses DataForSEO for keyword, SERP, backlink, and related SEO datasets; it also exposes MCP/agent integrations for compatible coding assistants.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, audits, issue results, tracked keywords, and historical observations live in the operator-controlled application database; keyword and SERP requests sent through DataForSEO leave the server and are retained/billed under that provider's account terms.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpenSEO needs paid third-party data and lacks SE Ranking's mature proprietary datasets, white-label reporting, competitor research, marketing plan, collaboration, and managed reliability.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert needs Docker, a database, authentication and email configuration, plus a funded DataForSEO account and API credentials, the rank tracker is not actually zero-cost to operate.

alternatives.name: SEO Panel
alternatives.desc: Rankings, audits, backlinks and reports in one venerable PHP dashboard; modernity was not part of the bargain.

facts.install: Upload the PHP application to a web server, create a MySQL database, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Sites, users, keyword positions, audit results, reports, logs, and plugin configuration live in the configured MySQL/MariaDB database; application code, cached files, exports, and configuration remain on the PHP host.
facts.gapVsPaid: SEO Panel's crawler, ranking collection, backlink data, interface, automation, and client-reporting workflow are substantially less mature and resilient than SE Ranking's.
facts.setupBlocker: The first hurdle is a traditional PHP/MySQL deployment with writable directories and cron jobs; after that, search-engine changes and third-party plugins make maintenance much more manual than Seobility.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SEO PowerSuite Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Four serious desktop modules, zero project saving on the free edition; useful for a snapshot, useless for tracking.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essential plan and a small owned-keyword tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for SE Ranking in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Playwright, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track a user-supplied keyword set, collect permitted search-result snapshots at low volume, combine them with user-supplied audit and backlink files, and show trends without recreating a commercial web index.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create projects with domains, keywords, target country, language, device, and tags.
Fetch rankings only through the configured compliant API and enforce a daily budget.
Store raw result snapshots and normalized positions so every chart is auditable.
Display current rank, movement, best rank, URL changes, and a compact SERP history.
Import backlink and keyword files from third-party tools without claiming independent coverage.
Add scheduled runs, failure alerts, CSV export, retention settings, and database backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out building a general web crawler or backlink index.
Deliberately leave out circumventing search-engine access controls.
Deliberately leave out traffic estimates presented as observed first-party data.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
